title: Shiver: Junji Ito Selected Stories
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A one-volume anthology of nine horror stories chosen by Junji Ito with his own notes, plus one new story (VIZ blurb via AniList and MU). Tales include a cursed record, a town stalked by floating balloon heads of its residents that try to noose them, a mansion of manipulated people, ancestors living as parasites on their descendants, and a story of body-horror holes (ANN reviewers).
life_message: No clear model of a good life is offered; the stories dwell on dread, obsession and the fragility of body and mind.

content.note: Grotesque, visceral imagery but less explicit than many adult action titles (ANN); Gore 83, Body Horror 83 (AniList); Blood and Gore, Murder, Cannibalism (MU).
Horror anthology that ANN reviewers call disturbing and nauseating, with warnings for trypophobia; Cosmic Horror, Curses, Ghost (AniList); Nightmare/s (MU).
No nudity mentioned by reviewers (ANN) (to verify).
'Hanging Blimp' centers on the pull of suicide, with nooses (ANN); Suicide/s, Hallucination/s, Memory Loss (MU).
Repeated noose and hanging imagery (ANN; MU Suicide/s); safe-messaging concern rather than instruction.

dominant: Cosmic and body horror; absurd dread; curses

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor codes; horror falls on ordinary people (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters are controlled by unseen forces in 'Marionette Mansion' (ANN), shown as horror.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family secrets and siblings recur (MU Family Secret, Brother and Sister).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Curses and ancestors drive stories (AniList Curses; ANN 'Honored Ancestors').

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Characters fight bodily survival against curses (AniList Body Horror).

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese ghost-story and curse traditions (kaidan) and ancestor reverence, turned into horror.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers describe the stories as enigmatic and unsettling, not message-driven (ANN).
delivery.note: The anthology offers mood and imagery rather than an argued worldview.

winners_losers: Most protagonists lose to curses, obsession or bodily transformation; no worldview is vindicated.
